Holds NO secret values — only commands that fetch them — so it lives next to the skill in git.

## Lookup order (first found wins; `--config` / `--skill` override)
1. `./.tmvp/config.yaml` (walking up from the cwd) · 2. the skill dir (`.agents/skills/<product>-tmvp/`)
3. `~/.tmvp/<product>/config.yaml` · 4. `~/.tmvp/config.yaml`. `tmvp config path` prints the pick.

## Shape
```yaml
version: 1
product: acme
assets: [assets, ../ops-repo/tmvp-assets]   # asset roots, searched in order (default [assets])
logging: { sink: file, path: ~/.tmvp/acme/logs }
server: { idle: 30m }
vars:    { region: ap-south-1 }              # ${vars.region}
secrets:                                     # named, lazy, held in server memory only
  ssh_key: "$file(sec get ACME_SSH_KEY --out ${out})"
envs:
  prod:
    destructive: false
    vars:    { domain: acme.com }            # env overrides top-level
    secrets: { db_ro: "$(op read op://Acme/prod-db/ro-dsn)" }
    systems:
      bastion:   { type: ssh, host: bastion.internal.example, user: deploy, key: "${file:secrets.ssh_key}" }
      db-tunnel: { type: portforward, via: bastion, remote: db.internal:5432 }
      db:
        type: postgres
        via: db-tunnel
        labels: { role: primary }
        read:  { dsn: "${secrets.db_ro}" }
        write: { dsn: "$file(sec get ACME_PROD_DB_RW --out ${out})" }   # inline $(…) is fine too
        limits: { rows: 500, statement_timeout: 10s }
      cloud:
        type: gcp
        project: acme-prod
        login: { manual: "gcloud auth login", check: "gcloud auth print-access-token" }
```

## Interpolation (after YAML parsing, per field — a value can never change structure)
| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `${vars.x}` | var (env vars override top-level) |
| `${secrets.x}` | named secret (env overrides top-level) |
| `${file:secrets.x}` | the secret as a FILE (whole field only): connectors get bytes in memory; external CLIs get a memfd (Linux) or 0600 temp file for that call only |
| `${NAME}` / `${NAME:-default}` | process environment variable, with default |
| `${user.x}` | left verbatim for web login steps (the named user's field) |
| `$$` | a literal `$` |

## Secrets are commands
- `"$(cmd args)"` — run (argv, no shell; `sh -c` only when it needs pipes), stdout captured in memory.
- `"$file(cmd --out ${out})"` — the command writes the private path `${out}`; tmvp reads and deletes it.
- A command may print `{"value":"…","expires_at":"RFC3339"}`; tmvp refetches before expiry.
- Run lazily on first use, held in the server's memory, redacted from all output. Refetched when the
  config changes or a credential is rejected (retried once; same value → `secret_invalid`).
- Literal values are rejected by `tmvp validate` in secret-ish fields: `dsn password passwd token key
  creds kubeconfig credentials secret uri api_key apikey private_key client_secret access_key
  secret_key`, and any URL with `user:password@`.

## Fields tmvp itself parses (per system)
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | connector type (required) — see `tmvp verbs` |
| `labels` | free `key: value`; select with `-l role=primary,team!=x`, `-l 'role in (a,b)'` |
| `via` | tunnel chain (ProxyJump semantics): `via: bastion` or `via: [jump1, db-tunnel]` — ssh, portforward or k8s systems in the same env; a docker container behind ssh: `via: [box, {container: pg}]` (`network:`, `sudo: true` optional; must follow an ssh hop, last) |
| `login` | `{manual: "<cmd the USER runs>", check: "<non-interactive cmd>"}`, or `{manual: browser}` for web |
| `destructive` | system-level override of the env flag |
| `limits` | `{rows, lines, bytes, timeout, statement_timeout, cost_per_second, rows_per_second, bytes_per_second, points_per_second, seq_scan_rows}` (defaults 1000 rows, 500 lines, 1 MiB, 10s, 15s). Also allowed at top level and per env; `timeout` precedence: `--timeout` > system > env > global > 10s — see `tmvp llms cost-and-timeouts` |
Everything else belongs to the type (`tmvp llms <type>`); `read.*` / `write.*` sub-maps hold the
credential per mode (write mode never falls back to `read.*`).

## Assets (saved items)
`assets:` lists asset roots relative to config.yaml (`~` expands). Each root holds
`<system>/<kind>/<name>.<ext>`: `queries/*.sql|*.json`, `scripts/*`, `pages/*.md` (+ `context.md`),
`apis/*.md`, `manifests/*.yaml`, `notes/`. Lookup goes root by root — the first match wins — so a
team repo can override a shared one. `tmvp <env> <system> ls` shows every item with its source file.
Every saved item starts with YAML front-matter (`description:` at least); `tmvp skill lint` checks it.

## Names
Env and system names must not contain `. , * ? [` or spaces and must not collide with each other,
with tmvp commands (`all write validate config check logs login secrets server version help new
skill export completion verbs envs systems llms`) or with a verb. `tmvp validate` reports it.
